title: The complete Crouzeix inequality
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that ||P[A]|| <= 2 max over the numerical range W(A) of ||P(z)|| for every complex square matrix A and every polynomial P with matrix coefficients of any size, with the sharp constant 2: the complete form of Crouzeix's conjecture. Convex domains with analytic polar boundaries approximate W(A) from outside; the Riemann map of the inverted exterior extends across the boundary; the Faber polynomials of the domain give a nonnegative kernel and a two-sided estimate of boundary norms by coefficients; the resolvent has positive Hermitian part on the circle, and testing it with the singular vectors of F[A] and the products FG and GF gives the constant 2.

units.title: The numerical range and the Crouzeix inequality
Faber polynomials and a positive kernel
The bound on a smooth convex domain

prerequisites: linear algebra over C: tensor products of matrices, Hermitian and positive semidefinite matrices, the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, singular vectors

complex analysis as in the core course Complex Analysis (Lebl's Guide to Cultivating Complex Analysis, cited by number at each use): Cauchy's integral formula and estimates, Laurent series, the residue theorem, Rouche's theorem, the open mapping theorem, the Riemann mapping theorem, harmonic conjugates and the reflection principle for harmonic functions
